evidence: Source-only row 52 review. The workbook check is Quality Checks!A53:D53; Internal Quality Checks!E53/G53 permits integration credentials during authoring with delivery stripping, while the skill excludes documented demo credentials and ${VAR} placeholders from secret findings. Frozen task/task.toml:30-35 contains the canonical OpenRouter endpoint, ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} interpolation and an empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not a live literal. task/instruction.md:15 explicitly publishes the Hireops!2026 demo password and seven hireops.example accounts. task/solution/app/src/db.js:126 labels the same password a public demo credential; there is no password/key field in either shipped seed JSON. The complete environment/assets/seed_data.json fixture has synthetic demo identities, .example emails (lines 44-86), ordinary compensation rows and empty per-record notes; its generated_note points to the operating instructions, with no grader-directed payload. Both seed copies have SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7. Security searches across all 35 frozen task files found no live-key signature, private-key block, author Windows/macOS/Linux home path, database connection credential, or prompt-injection directive. The reviewed URL/credential matches were the canonical provider endpoint, localhost probes, documentation and demo/session implementation. Runtime /app, /assets, /instructions, /tests, /root/.codex and /usr/local paths are container contract paths, not author-host paths. The solution network-call scan found only the local worker proxy (task/solution/app/src/bootstrap.js:28-30, hostname 127.0.0.1) and the browser API wrapper (public/js/app.js:46-53); public/index.html:53-54 loads local scripts. No task-added remote script downloader or external data endpoint was found. Dockerfile network installation is the required frozen template: environment/Dockerfile SHA256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1 and tests/Dockerfile SHA256 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd each match their frozen template byte-for-byte; npm/pip versions are explicit. The template OS-image tags and apt steps are preserved shared policy, and public browser CDN permission is an explicit profile exception, not a task-authored security defect. Adversarial scope check: an otherwise polished app could conceal a live key or exfiltration URL in its source while passing a UI-only smoke test; this review included the entire shipped task tree and inspected credential/network matches rather than relying on UI behavior. No such concrete candidate payload was found. Conforming alternative considered: an app using the documented demo password and permitted external fonts must not fail this row solely for those strings/network choices; the skill/profile expressly permits them. All 35 scanned task hashes, eight cited frozen rule/template hashes and four policy/context hashes were recomputed and matched manifest.json.
